Chapter 6: The Myths of Vulnerability — Unraveling Old Stories.
Have you ever been told that being vulnerable is a sign of weakness? It’s such a common message—whether we hear it at home, in the office, or just pick it up from the world around us. There’s this old story that says, if you let your guard down, you’ll end up hurt, dismissed, or even taken advantage of.
But, as life goes on, those stories start to fall apart.
Picture a seasoned executive. She’s always been proud of her cool composure—she keeps her emotions out of the boardroom, no matter what. But then, a personal crisis hits, and that emotional armor slips. One afternoon, she decides to open up to a trusted colleague. She braces herself for judgment or pity, but instead, she’s met with real understanding. Their conversation goes deeper than she expected, and suddenly, she doesn’t feel so alone. That old myth—that vulnerability equals weakness—starts to unravel, right then and there.
There’s another story that gets passed around: vulnerability means oversharing, like telling every secret or emotion to anyone who’ll listen. But true vulnerability isn’t about pouring your heart out to everyone. It’s about making a choice—to be open with the right people, at the right time, for the right reasons. It’s not about looking for attention or approval; it’s about building a real connection.
Think about a young man wrestling with anxiety. He wonders if he should tell his friends, but he’s scared they’ll see him differently. When he finally decides to share, he picks a quiet moment and talks to someone he really trusts. The friend just listens—and you can almost feel the relief. That conversation doesn’t fix everything, but it opens a door. The myth that being vulnerable is reckless, or just a way to get attention, starts to fade away.
There’s also this belief that vulnerability is only for certain people—artists, therapists, or those going through a crisis. But, honestly, everyone faces moments that call for courage. Whether you’re asking for help, admitting you made a mistake, or expressing love, vulnerability is part of everyday life.
Most of us don’t realize just how much these myths shape the choices we make. We hold back, waiting for that moment when it finally feels safe to be real. But, here’s the thing—that moment rarely just shows up. It’s only when we start to question these old stories, take small risks, and notice what happens, that new possibilities begin to show up.
This isn’t about throwing caution to the wind or ignoring healthy boundaries. It’s about seeing that strength and vulnerability aren’t opposites—they actually work together. When you’re willing to be seen, to risk rejection or failure, you open the door to real growth.
And as these old myths lose their hold, a new story starts to take shape. It’s a story where vulnerability isn’t something to hide, but a source of connection, creativity, and resilience. The journey isn’t over—it’s ongoing—but every step you take brings a deeper sense of freedom and a stronger feeling of belonging.
